_comment: Failure-criteria thresholds for the uSTOL Monte Carlo dashboard. EDIT THESE VALUES. The dashboard build (build_dashboard_data.py) reads this file and grades every case. Delete/rename the file or set enabled=false to turn the whole feature off.
_instructions: kind: 'scalar' (one value per case, immediate ok/fail) | 'timeseries' (per-sample signal vs bounds, with a grace interval) | 'oscillation' (per-phase control-command activity + spectrum).
severity: 'critical' (a sustained breach makes the case FAIL) | 'degraded' (a sustained breach makes it PARTIAL).
bounds: give 'min' and/or 'max', or 'max_abs' for a symmetric +/- limit. Units: deg, deg/s, m, m/s, g (load factor), m/s (sink).
phase (timeseries): restrict the check to one flight phase label as written in *_flight.csv (GROUND/CLIMB/CRUISE/APPROACH/FLARE/ROLLOUT/LOITER). Omit = whole flight.
grace_s (timeseries): the longest CONTINUOUS time the signal may stay out of bounds and still be only 'flag'ged (not failed). 0 = any excursion fails. e.g. grace_s=1.0 -> a <=1 s spike is tolerated.

oscillation: 'phases' lists which (long) phases get a frequency spectrum; time-domain activity (RMS, reversal_rate, slew_sat) is computed for EVERY phase flown so short phases (FLARE/GROUND) are still scored. 'min_samples' (default 64) gates the spectrum. 'rms_min' suppresses flags when the control barely moves. NOTE: 10 Hz logging => only oscillation below ~5 Hz (Nyquist) is visible.
metric (scalar): the per-case metric name computed by build_dashboard_data.py (e.g. ground_roll_m, td_sink_mps, td_pitch_deg, Vlof_mps, max_AoA_deg).

Any criterion whose signal/metric/phase is unavailable for a campaign is reported 'na' (neutral) and never fails a case. Tune every threshold below to your real limits — the values shipped here are placeholders seeded from the mission setpoints (cruise 100 m / 12 m/s, etc.).

criteria._climb_note: climb_pitch/climb_rate are scoped to the ESTABLISHED climb via gate_signal=alt_agl_m in [5,90] m: below 5 m is the rotation transient (pitch ramps 0->16) and above 90 m is the level-off to the 100 m cruise (pitch->0) — judging those boundaries would falsely flag every case. Adjust gate_max if cruise_alt changes.
criteria._load_factor_note: Uses the SIM-LOGGED load factor (result.json max_load_factor_total / min_load_factor_nz) — reliable, unlike the kinematic d(V)/dt estimate which spikes at ground contact. Only present in the mix campaign; 'na' (neutral) for campaigns that don't log it.
criteria._envelope_comment: Flight-envelope limits from FDM_LAT/flight_envelopes.m: the safe (V,gamma) region is where steady trim needs AoA in [-5,10] deg, elevator in [-10,10] deg, and trim throttle in [0.3,0.9]. We check the ACTUAL logged signals directly (more faithful than the steady-trim (V,gamma) polygon for a dynamic run). Limits are flap-independent.
criteria._envelope_Vgamma_comment: Operating-point check: V (TAS) must stay inside the safe airspeed band [Vlo(gamma), Vhi(gamma)] from flight_envelopes.m (exported to safe_envelope_cfg32.csv). Out-of-band = the (V,gamma) point left the gray safe region. NOTE: cfg32 = flap 20 (STOL); if cruise flies flap 0, export safe_envelope_cfg18.csv and add a second criterion scoped to CRUISE. Set severity to critical once you trust the flap match.
criteria._envelope_phasewise_comment: Phase-wise V-gamma envelope: the SAME membership test scoped to one phase, so you can see which phase leaves the safe band and tune grace/severity per phase. IMPORTANT — the band depends on FLAP, which varies by phase: set 'envelope_file' per phase to match (cfg18 = flap 0 clean; cfg32 = flap 20 high-lift). Only cfg32 is exported so far, so these default to it; export safe_envelope_cfg18.csv from flight_envelopes.m and switch whichever phases fly clean (typically CLIMB/CRUISE). 'safe_envelope_Vgamma' above stays as the whole-flight catch-all.
criteria._oscillation_comment: Per axis the VERDICT is driven by the COMMAND channel (controller-actionable). 'companions' add the ACTUAL surface deflection and the body rate as diagnostics (role=actual/rate) for the command-vs-response view: high command band-power => controller is commanding oscillation (fix in controller); high actual/rate with clean command => airframe/actuator self-oscillation (fix structurally). Only <~5 Hz is observable at 10 Hz logging.
